title: Club life and volunteering
summary: The club is the heart of the sport. How to join in, how to help at competitions as a volunteer, and why volunteers matter so much.

body.html: Many shooters start at a club. A club is a place to practise, but it is also a community. People share advice, travel to competitions together, celebrate wins and support each other after a bad day.

Clubs run their own events, from friendly weekend shoots to stages of a national championship. A national federation may even hand a club the running of an international event, but the federation stays responsible for it. All of this depends on people.

Volunteers do a lot at a competition. They register shooters, fill the traps with targets, help with parking and food, take photos for the club and clear up cases and target fragments. Some help with the score sheets where the rules allow it, always under the referee's eye.
Some jobs, such as working as a trapper next to a trap, start with a safety briefing. Wear hearing protection and safety glasses, and follow the instructions of the ground.

Want to get involved? Ask your club who needs help. Volunteering is a good way to meet people and to see how a competition works from the inside. It is also a good first step towards refereeing or becoming an organiser: How to become a referee.

A good club member follows the ground rules, pays fees on time, helps beginners and joins clean-up days. One of the kindest things you can do for a newcomer is to show them the safety rules and invite them to shoot with you.
Thinking of running a shoot yourself? Step by step: How to run a club shoot.

key_points.html: A club is a community, not only a practice ground.
Jobs near a trap start with a safety briefing, hearing protection and glasses.
Volunteering is a good first step towards refereeing or organising.
Help beginners and follow the ground rules.

did_you_know.html: At a big competition tens of thousands of targets may be thrown in a day, and someone has to load each of them into a trap.

quiz.q: Who keeps the scorecard in Sporting™?

options.text: The referee, or a helper under the referee's eye
Only the shooter who is on the stand

quiz.explain: In Sporting™ the referee fills in the scorecard or chooses someone to do it under supervision.

quiz.q: What is a good first step towards becoming a referee?

options.text: Buy a referee card online, with no exam
Win a club shoot, then ask to referee
Help at club shoots, then take a course

quiz.explain: Helping at club shoots shows you the work from the inside. Then your federation's course and exam lead to a referee certificate.

quiz.q: Can a federation hand a club the running of a competition?

options.text: Yes, but the federation stays responsible
No, only FITASC may run events
Yes, and then nobody is responsible

quiz.explain: A federation may hand the running of an event to a club, but it stays responsible for applying the rules.
